results.summary_before: This design implements an 8-bit configurable Galois linear-feedback shift register (LFSR). It has three modes: normal shift, set shift register, and set XOR mask, allowing the user to configure the feedback polynomial. Data is loaded 4 bits at a time over two cycles, and the full 8-bit state is available on the outputs. The documentation is minimal, but the pin names and description indicate the basic operation.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit multiplier that processes two 8-bit numbers in 4-bit chunks (nibbles) over multiple clock cycles. It uses a valid signal to latch each nibble sequentially, and a toggle bit to select which half of the 16-bit result is output on the 8-bit output pins. The multiplication is performed in a bit-serial fashion, requiring several clock cycles per operation. The design is notable for its minimal interface and chunked processing approach.
